_comment: Feature manifest — the regression lock's human-auditable checklist.
Every shipped user-visible capability appears here and names the test that
owns it. regression_tests verifies each named test symbol still exists in
its source file, so deleting a test fails the build. Add an entry whenever
a phase ships something a user can see; never delete one without a written
Node-level and attribute-level coverage is handled separately and
exhaustively by nodes.txt / attributes.txt — this file is for capabilities.

features.description: Owned terrain snapshots prepare placement, picking and conservative patch bounds off-thread; pending requests coalesce and stale results cannot replace the latest terrain
Autosave snapshots with a nonblocking graph lock, writes a temporary file off-thread, atomically replaces the recovery slot, and flushes on shutdown
Reusable workers preserve band boundaries, support nested and concurrent calls, and propagate exceptions without deadlock

Input and ready uploads precede viewport draws; secondary images are reused between deadlines, shadows and instance streams are shared, GPU timestamp envelopes coexist with pass timers, and real-context captures preserve the image
Timeline panel: transport, loop range, scrub bar, per-attribute keyframing with key markers and interpolation choice; set_time and set_key AI ops; tracks were already serialized with their attributes

EcoSystem-style mesh scattering: a mesh object bound to any Points node draws instanced copies standing on the terrain, seeded yaw and size jitter, Properties picker, set_scatter and import_object AI ops, binding persists with node-id remap
Quilt: Efros-Freeman patch resynthesis - hashed candidate patches auditioned against the laid overlap, feathered joins, bit-identical per seed
MeanShift mode-seeking smoothing, SetBorders rim pinning, SelectBlobs difference-of-gaussians blob detection
DiffusionLimited: branching dendrites by particle aggregation, hashed walk (bit-identical), age-tapered relief, stickiness and smoothing controls
GaborNoise: sparse convolution of oriented cosine kernels under a gaussian envelope, anisotropy from locked streaks to isotropic grain, octave stacking
ExportPoints (CSV or PLY, with terrain height baked in) and PointsFromCsv import; the CSV roundtrip is exact
Landform set pieces: island, mountain, caldera, rift valley and mesa, noise-wobbled rims and ridged flanks
KMeans terrain zoning over height+slope (or a second feature map), seeded init, fixed Lloyd iterations, clusters relabeled by mean height so mask A is always the lowest zone
Paths as ordered point clouds: PointsToPath (nearest-neighbor tour), PathResample, PathFractalize (midpoint wander), PathSDF, and PathCarve accepts a connected path input
MakeTileable: separable periodic cosine crossfade with the half-offset copy, so the tile wraps seamlessly; feather sharpens the crossfade
SelectMidrange (gaussian band over the height range), SelectTransitions (where two surfaces trade places), SelectBorder (EDT band along a mask boundary, inward/outward/both)
IQ (slope-damped), Jordan (gradient-warped squared) and Pingpong (folded) fBm variants on the Noise node
Kuwahara edge-preserving smoothing, DirectionalBlur, Detrend (best-fit plane removal), RelativeElevation and SmoothFill
Flood: standing water at a set level, everywhere-below or edge-connected (walled basins stay dry); outputs surface, depth and mask
Morphology (dilate/erode/open/close/gradient/top hat/black hat, square or octagon element), AreaRemove blob pruning, and Zhang-Suen Skeleton
Point-cloud domain: ScatterPoints (random, jittered grid, spaced), PointsRelax, PointsFilter (mask band + keep chance), PointsToMask stamps and PointsSDF distance, all deterministic
PathCarve: a drawn polyline, Chaikin-smoothed, stamped and distance-fielded, carving riverbeds, roads and canyons (negative depth builds walls), graded along the line
FieldShape (8 analytic waveforms with a GPU mirror) and Curve (a drawn tone curve for elevations through the gradient editor)
Autosave every two minutes when the history has moved, three slots in rotation, and crash recovery offering the newest slot back after an unclean exit
Exact Euclidean distance transform (Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher), plus Median and Equalize filters

A project file carries the whole scene - meshes with transforms and material bindings, cameras with lenses and render assignments, layers, selection - and the whole environment, with node-id bindings remapped through the graph loader's id map
Priority-Flood depression filling: lakes as filled-minus-original, and flow routing that no longer dead-ends in every hollow
Cellular (Worley) noise in the field domain: F1, F2, seam distance and flat cell value, three metrics, mirrored exactly in GLSL
Dragging a wire onto empty canvas offers only nodes that can take it, then wires the new node up
Planets and the infinite ground plane are shaped by a field graph, transpiled to GLSL and spliced into the planet shader
Self-registering node registry with categories and descriptions
Dirty-tracked evaluation: clean nodes are not recomputed, dirt flows downstream only
Cycles are rejected when a link would create one
Same seed reproduces bit-identical terrain; different seed differs
Graph round-trips through JSON with attributes and links intact
Droplet and pipe-model hydraulic erosion, stream power (explicit + implicit), all preserve relief and stay bounded
Slope/altitude/curvature/cavity masks and logic nodes output normalized [0,1] masks
Terragen/Gaea-class surface pack: power fractal, stratify, craggy, fake stones, snow, rivers, coast
A whole authored workflow reproduces bit-identically across runs
Grit, Gravel, Peaks, Sharpen, Cracks, Glaciation, Dissolve, TerrainClip — all deterministic, Dissolve emits a flow map, TerrainClip flattens and emits a hole mask
TerrainSculpt is a non-destructive layer: unpainted is a passthrough, strokes raise the surface, stroke mask marks edits, painted field survives save/load
Terrain texture, splatmap, splat material and PBR derivation produce finite textures with no node errors
Material graph: MaterialOutput plus channel nodes evaluate as a chain
A material subgraph saves to and loads from the library with fresh node ids
Real camera optics: sensor formats, FOV from focal length, EV100 and the exposure triangle, film stocks
AI graph spec builder tolerates unknown types, label strings and markdown fences; registry catalog lists nodes and attributes
Planetary relief is deterministic, bounded, continuous over the sphere with no seams, seed-dependent, and silenced by zero coverage
Undo/redo of node add/delete, attribute edits and links
Attribute values and links are restored exactly by undo and re-applied by redo
World settings (sun, fog) participate in the same undo history
Scene objects and the active camera are restored by undo
Imported mesh vertices survive an undo round trip bit-identically while being shared between snapshots
A new edit discards the redo branch
Named history list with jump-to-any-point
History cap trims oldest steps without corrupting the position
Terrain after an undo recomputes bit-identically to before the edit
Multiple planets coexist with auto-placement, each with surface layers; ground-plane layers are separate; all undoable
Planets and infinite terrain layers survive save/load with parenting intact
No node type may ever be removed or change category
No node attribute may be removed or change type
Committed projects re-evaluate to the same bits
Every manifest feature names a test that still exists
Field domain: per-point evaluation with no resolution, standard inputs, deterministic, type-permissive, LOD-aware
Rasterize and Sample bridge the field and raster domains: a field can be eroded, and a buffer can drive a shader
Field graphs compile to GLSL: shared nodes emitted once, samplers declared, unsupported nodes rejected loudly. Every field node must have an emitter or the contract suite fails.
Any node can be bypassed: the graph is evaluated as though it were not there, through chains, in both domains, and it survives save/load
Grouping a selection into a MetaNode does not change what the graph computes, and ungrouping restores it exactly
MetaNode parameters can be published with their real type and range, drive the inner graph, and survive save/load
Any terrain-transforming node can have its effect confined by a blend mask, provided by the graph rather than per node; unconnected it is a no-op
A MetaNode can be saved to a personal library and dropped into any project as a reusable node, keeping its inner graph, exposed parameters and their tuned values
A Node List view of the same graph, rooted at the terrain result with inputs indented beneath, per-row bypass, and unreachable nodes listed separately
Every parameter can carry an animation track; scene time drives them, they survive save/load, reach the field domain, and cost nothing when unused
Redirect shader: any vector field moves where any other field is evaluated, giving warp, flow and domain distortion on anything, on CPU and GPU alike

Displacement shader family: along normal / up / vector / fixed direction, depth in real units or relative, smoothing, quality boost and displace-outwards-only, with both a displaced height and a 3D offset output
Compute Normal recovers the surface direction after displacement by central differences, so downstream nodes see the displaced shape rather than the flat plane underneath
Zones confine one field to a sphere or box region with a smooth fade, and expose the region itself as a mask output
Texture coordinates as a field input, with plane choice, scale, rotation and offset

The transpiler re-emits a subtree under a second evaluation point, so warped and finite-differenced graphs are correct on the GPU instead of silently reusing the un-redirected value; generated variables are always declared before use
The GPU mirrors FieldValue's permissive conversions exactly: a number broadcasts to a vector, a vector read as a number is its length, a colour is its luminance
D8 flow accumulation: how much water passes through each point, computed over the whole surface with a deterministic total ordering
Topographic wetness index ln(a/tan b) — high in flat hollows fed from above, low on steep ground, finite even on perfectly flat terrain
Terrain resolution operations: half, quarter, double or custom sampling with smooth or nearest interpolation, changing detail without changing buffer size

A TerrainDisplacement node compiles its field graph to GLSL and the viewport evaluates it per vertex, with normals following the displaced surface; a graph that fails to link keeps the previous program instead of blanking the viewport
A node-editor view file with non-finite or absurd values is discarded rather than loaded, because one made the application spin behind a black window on every launch, permanently

Environment-sensitive distribution: where a material belongs by altitude, steepness and facing, each with a soft band, combined multiplicatively, and read after displacement so it describes the displaced surface
Colour blending in the field domain — mix, add, multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten — with the factor meaning the same thing in every mode

A TerrainSurface node shades the viewport terrain per pixel from a colour field, sharing one shader program with the displacement — the prelude is emitted once per stage and stripped from every function after the first
The assistant, the Python API and MCP can set colour and gradient parameters; an rgb triple sets a colour, a single number is a grey, and gradient stops are sorted
Every link in a golden project must actually connect, so a golden cannot silently lock a graph with half its links dropped by a wrong port name
Every golden project must produce varying output, so a golden cannot silently lock a flat buffer

Field type converters: colour/vector/texcoord split and combine, FieldToNumber/Color/Vector/TexCoord adapters with explicit lane and plane choices, HSV in both directions, FieldColorAdjust; FieldVectorOp gains a full vector output; every converter mirrors FieldValue's conversion rules and has a GLSL twin
Every field output port of every node (not only the first) has a GLSL emitter that produces its own expression; secondary outputs cannot silently fall back to the primary on the GPU

Node families for every major component with their own workspace: Light (LightSource + planned area/sky/gel/volumetric/flare), Camera (SceneCamera, CameraPath + planned), Animation (Oscillator, TimeRemap, AnimationSequence + planned), Scene (ImportObject, Primitive, Planet, InfiniteTerrain + planned), Cloud (planned P5 set), Render (RenderOutput, RenderPasses, RenderBackdrop, PostProcess + planned); planned nodes carry their roadmap phase as attributes and are configuration nodes in the contract

Render editor state saved with the project and covered by undo: backdrop dome (file, 7 mappings, rotation, exposure, tint, blend, haze, sun flag), pass mask, beauty format, render defaults, post-processing; scene objects remember the graph node that drives them, remapped through the node id map on load

True HDR image files: OpenEXR scanline read (NONE/RLE/ZIPS/ZIP, HALF/FLOAT/UINT) and write (FLOAT, uncompressed), Radiance .hdr read/write, LDR formats loaded as linear light; backs the backdrop dome and the render passes

One-click installers: install.bat (Windows, winget), install.command (macOS, Homebrew), scripts/install.sh (Linux, apt/dnf/pacman) each check the toolchain, fetch dependencies, build, and install per user with shortcuts; POSIX twins of get_deps/build/test/start

Distributable packages: Inno Setup .exe and portable .zip for Windows (per-user, no elevation, .gpxt association, clean uninstall), .app bundle and .dmg for macOS (ad-hoc signed, icns generated with sips/iconutil); binaries stripped for shipping with the debug symbols kept beside them

macOS and Linux support: OpenGL 4.1 core context and #version 410 shaders on Apple, POSIX file dialogs (osascript/zenity/kdialog), signal-based crash reports with backtrace, BSD-socket Ollama client with chunked decoding, fork/exec render process control, pipe-based console capture, per-user data directory for preferences, layout and node-editor views
Every registered node satisfies the universal contract: ports typed, attributes labelled and in range, deterministic, finite, serializable

Realistic terrain layer (type 3): eroded ridged mountains in upland belts, eroded hills, terraced plateaus, carved valleys with wetness, lowland lakes below the water level; CPU heightf with float octaves, mirrored in PL_FN and checked by planet_gpu_verify

Stable tile-on-sphere placement (gpx::planet::sphere_place / pl_sphere_place): keeps terrain height at 1e12-radius planets, wraps the tile with heights shrinking on sub-tile planets; radius range 0.1 mm to 1e12 m in UI and API

Terrain tile placed onto the planet surface at upload (studio/planet_place.cpp): planet relief shows through flat ground, is levelled under features (flatten), feathered footprints and border, holes become water-filled basins; cached relief, place_* settings persisted and scriptable

Named window layouts: the whole arrangement (ImGui's dock state, which viewports are open, what each shows, which panels are open, the extra node editors) saved by name to <settings>/layouts/*.json and loaded back; View > Layouts, plus save_layout/load_layout/delete_layout/list_layouts/reset_layout ops and MCP tools

Viewports are a set of up to 8 windows rather than a count of 1-6: add, close, split right/down and arrange 1-8 cells without rebuilding the layout, each view closable from its own tab, the last one never closable; arrange_views/add_view/close_view ops

Mesh diagnosis ported from Meshwright (MIT): 11 checks - open holes and boundary loops, non-manifold edges, face winding, inside-out normals, degenerate and duplicate faces, duplicate and unused vertices, slivers, separate shells, unusual scale - each with a count, a severity and sampled locations, plus volume, area, Euler number, genus, bounds and a 0-100 readiness score with a verdict

Staged mesh repair: junk geometry, welding, winding, inside-out flip and hole filling by boundary loop, repeated until the mesh stops changing then re-analysed from scratch, with a before/after table; small-shell removal is opt-in and never deletes every shell
Quadric edge-collapse decimation to a triangle target (Vue's Decimate, p306), with the worst surface deviation measured against the original by point-to-triangle distance rather than estimated
Mesh file formats written by hand with no dependency: OBJ, STL (binary and ascii), PLY (ascii and binary little-endian) and OFF, read and written, polygons fanned to triangles on load

Mesh Tools panel and the Objects tool row: import, analyse, repair, reduce, split into shells and export, with issue locations marked in the viewport, a file-units selector, a measured repair report and an export that warns when the mesh is not a closed solid; import_mesh/mesh_analyse/mesh_repair/mesh_reduce/mesh_split/mesh_export ops and MCP tools

Optional mesh engines behind engine/gpx/mesh_engines.hpp: Manifold v3.5.2 (Apache-2.0) gives guaranteed-manifold solid reconstruction and unions overlapping shells into one solid, running as repair stage 5 when our own stages cannot close the surface; a build without the engine disables the stage and says so in the repair notes rather than degrading silently

Quad retopology with QuadriFlow (BSD-3): rebuilds a surface as evenly sized, curvature-aligned quads rather than thinning the triangles it was given, triangulated on the way back; built without Boost by pointing QuadriFlow's library-backed max-flow solvers at its own dependency-free one (scripts/patch_quadriflow.py), so the only dependency is header-only Eigen

Optical simulation per camera (Vue's Advanced Camera Options, p333): one switch, then lens distortion that follows the focal length and sensor (barrel wide, pincushion long) or is dialled by hand, vignetting scaled from the aperture, lateral chromatic aberration, shutter-driven camera-motion blur and an optional lens flare that only appears while the sun is in frame - applied as a post pass to the viewport, the Preview panel and captured images, and skipped entirely when off

Every workspace keeps its own window arrangement (layouts/workspace-<name>), captured on leaving and restored on entering; the Materials workspace has its own default: Material Studio on top, Material Browser beneath, node graph and scene view below, Properties and Outliner on the right

Material Studio: one material with New/Load/Save, its type (Simple, PBR textures, Mixed, Layered, Distribution, Effector - read from the graph and set by scaffolding nodes), a live preview per material (sphere/cube/flat, three backgrounds, turntable) rendered from a per-material texture cache that re-uploads only when the material changed, every channel and surface property, the layer stack, and an unsaved-changes prompt when switching materials

Material Browser with Project and Library tabs: thumbnails, hover cards with a larger preview and what the material is made of, double-click to open in the studio, right-click to assign, save or move to the library trash (never delete)

Two material types beyond colour: DistributionLayer, whose presence mask also places objects (a deterministic hashed dart throw with spacing, threshold and size-from-presence, the EcoSystem-material idea), and EffectorLayer, a typed influence field (pressure, wind, light, heat, moisture, custom) with strength, falloff, invert and an optional tint so it can be seen while painted - published for systems that arrive later

The asset index (engine/asset_index.cpp): scans watched roots by kind and extension, keys records as kind/relative-path, keeps tags and notes across rescans, finds a PNG beside a file as its thumbnail, searches by TF-IDF cosine over name, folders, tags, note and kind with prefix matching for words still being typed and a kind filter, trashes by moving to <root>/trash (never deleting) and restores, and round-trips through one JSON file
Asset words: lower-cased, split on punctuation, CamelCase and letter/digit boundaries; single letters dropped; file names prettified (Moss_Rock_02 -> Moss Rock 02)

The Assets tab of the Material Browser: a search box that reorders tiles by match, a kind filter, trash view, hover cards with tags and note, double-click opens (a material loads and opens in the studio, a mesh imports, a layout applies), right-click tags/notes/trashes/restores, and a Folders popup to add, remove and rescan roots; the material library and the layouts folder are watched by default

Asset ops for the assistant, Python API and MCP: asset_search (selects the Assets tab with the query), asset_open, asset_tag/untag/note, asset_trash/restore, asset_rescan, asset_roots, asset_add_root/remove_root; and material ops open_material, list_materials, set_material_type, save_material, load_material - every one an MCP tool (studio_asset_tools.py)

Every surface property a material carries, declared on MaterialOutput in Vue's tab groups (Color: tint, brightness, saturation, map scale, origin; Bump: normal intensity, bump depth, slope dependence, invert, displacement depth and smoothing; Highlights: GGX/Phong model, intensity, roughness, highlight colour, anisotropy; Transparency: amount, refraction index, turn reflective with angle, fade out, thin surface, additive, flare; Reflection: reflectivity, minimal reflectivity, angle sensitivity, blur, metalness; Translucency: amount, subsurface scattering with depth, balance and colour, backlight; Effects: diffuse/ambient split, luminous with colour, contrast, casts shadows, colour reflected and transmitted light) and read into one MaterialParams struct with clamping and defaults for old files

The terrain and the material preview shade from the same MaterialParams through one shared GLSL snippet (renderer_matparams.cpp): tint/gain/saturation on the albedo, contrast on the light falloff, F0 from highlight intensity, colour and refraction index, Fresnel with minimal reflectivity and angle sensitivity, Phong as an alternative highlight model, translucency with scattering colour and backlight, luminous emission, diffuse/ambient balance, colour-reflected light, bump depth and invert on the normal map

The Material Studio's properties as Vue's tabs - Color, Bump, Highlights, Transparency, Reflection, Translucency, Effects - each control generated from the node's attribute (label, range, tooltip in one place), every channel with a mode combo (None disconnects, Picture adds a TextureFile from a file dialog, Procedural adds a FractalColor) and an edit button to the node; Layers, Population, Effector or Mix tabs appear with the material's type and edit the layer or driving node in place

The Material Studio laid out as Vue's Advanced Material Editor: preview with object/background/spin, Randomize, Zoom and Store (snapshots restored by double-click into the same MaterialOutput); name, type, mapping and the material options popup; the material hierarchy with three-state visibility (visible, invisible, highlighted in a solid colour) and Add/Remove/Up/Down; tabs for the selected line - Color, Alpha, Bump, Displacement, Highlights, Transparency, Reflection, Translucency, Effects (with Global transformation), PBR's Ambient Occlusion, Metalness, Roughness, Clearcoat; a layer's Color/Alpha/Bump/Highlights/Effects/Presence; a mix's Materials to mix / Alpha / Influence of environment

Every channel has Vue's mode: Constant/None, Mapped picture (a TextureFile with load, rotate, invert, mirror, gamma, scale, offset, interpolation), Procedural (any node; FractalColor by default) and Natural grain (two colours through a noise: scale, roughness, contrast, balance, distortion) - each switch rewires the graph and never deletes the node it replaces

A layer's Presence: altitude band by terrain, absolute or relative to sea, slope band, orientation, alpha boost that strengthens but never invents; Mixed material: two materials by one distribution against the proportions inside a smooth blending strip, five blending methods, influence of altitude (signed), slope (signed) and orientation (azimuth)

The configuration manager: config.json with AI services (key, endpoint, model, enabled), ComfyUI (local/cloud, mode, install path, workflow folders, poll, timeout), AI defaults (text/image/3D providers, output folders), external applications, shortcuts; secrets protected with DPAPI per user (marked plain elsewhere); provider defaults filled in; a garbage file fails with a reason, an empty one loads every default

Keyboard shortcuts as a table of commands with default chords, remapped from Settings > Shortcuts by pressing keys, conflicts flagged, Reset per command; chords parse and format as exact inverses; the toolbar asks by command id

The Settings window: General, Shortcuts, AI services (defaults + a row per provider with hidden key, endpoint, model, ready state), ComfyUI (connection check), Applications, Asset folders; Preferences moved into it

AI services ported from Image Express as C++: one HTTP client (WinHTTP; POSIX sockets elsewhere), text through Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini; images through OpenAI Images, Stability v2beta, Google Imagen and ComfyUI; 3D through Meshy (preview then refine), Tripo and Hitem3D (ak:sk token exchange); every request builder and parser a pure function tested on the documented JSON with error mutations; results written to disk before anyone is told; poll backoff 2 s to 15 s

ComfyUI client: probe /object_info, queue /prompt with a client id, poll /history, fetch /view; parameters injected by (node id, input name) with empty values leaving workflow defaults and a missing node named in the error; bindings inferred from node classes and titles; workflows found by name in the install and configured folders, else the bundled SDXL text_to_image

Prompt templates written for terrain work: a texture as a seamless top-down flat-lit tile, a skydome as a 2:1 equirectangular panorama with the horizon at the middle, negatives merged, sizes forced (square tiles, 2:1 skies at least 2048 wide)

AI jobs on a worker thread with progress, cancel and a result serviced on the UI thread: the file joins the asset index; a texture connects to a material's channel, a skydome becomes the backdrop, a model imports as an object; Generate image / Generate 3D model / Jobs windows; the AI menu and Objects tool row

Natural language for the whole scene, the terrain or the atmosphere: a planner prompt over every action schema plus the generation ops, an answer that is a JSON list of actions applied through ai_apply_actions; the assistant bars now use the configured text provider
Binary glTF read natively (geometry, node transforms, uint8/16/32 indices, every primitive welded) so the models the 3D services return import without a library; a non-GLB fails with a reason

Object deformers in the object's own space (gpx/deform.hpp): twist about each axis growing along it (Vue's Twist), bend as a progressive rotation about an axis from the base, skew sliding the top by a fraction of the width, taper narrowing or widening the top; identity leaves points alone; deformed normals from two deformed tangents; the mesh vertex shader is the GLSL twin and the exports bake the same function

Gizmo tools for every scene object: Move, Rotate, Scale, and for meshes Twist (dashed rings), Bend (half rings), Skew (diamonds), Taper (centre dial); shortcuts W E R T B K J; the tool's name beside the gadget; Vue's Show Gizmos switch (Ctrl+G, tool row and View menu) and a per-object switch in Properties; every number the gadgets drag is typed in the Properties Deform block with a reset

Deformers and the per-object gizmo switch in the scene file, written only when set so older files and undeformed objects are unchanged; place_object sets the whole transform (heading, pitch, bank, squeeze) and the deformers by name

A narrow status bar along the bottom: the status line on the left and, right-aligned, FPS shown and possible, the frame's breakdown (CPU work, interface, views, GPU), the last evaluation with node and patch counts, process memory (peak) and free system memory, CPU share, VRAM used/total (NVIDIA/AMD extensions), the GPU name, and the governor's state; every figure has a tooltip; the same figures and every marked phase are in the API state file

The performance governor: thresholds in Settings (main and secondary view fps); it judges the work per frame, not the capped rate, and steps down after 0.7 s slow - secondary views' render scale and the preview panel first, then shadows and cloud quality in secondary views, then the main view's scale and the terrain subdivision - and steps up after 4 s comfortable, never two steps within a second; nothing it changes is saved

The tile is re-placed onto the planet only when the layers or placement settings change: the key hashes fields, not struct bytes - hashing a struct with padding made it differ every frame and cost 9 ms of re-placement and re-upload per frame; the UI snapshot is likewise rebuilt only on a change, a pointer press or a quarter second

A mesh object (primitive or imported) assigned a MaterialOutput (Objects/Materials panel, or the assign_material op with an object name) is lit by the same GGX PBR pipeline the terrain uses - roughness, metallic, specular, reflection, clearcoat, translucency, emissive, ambient from the sky colours - through the shared MATERIAL_UNIFORMS_PLACEHOLDER/MATERIAL_FN_PLACEHOLDER snippets; an unassigned mesh keeps the old flat-lit look via MaterialParams defaults. Picture-mapped textures still need a UV channel on the mesh format, which this phase does not add - see AGENTS.md

Cinema 4D-styled vector icon set: thin line glyphs with rounded joins on the 18 / 26 / 36 px palette ladder (prefs icon_size), pixel-snapped so the 18 px set is crisp, filled silhouettes for object types, visibility dots, transport and key marks, deformers; every id paints, stays in its box and is deterministic

The Objects panel as a Cinema 4D Object Manager: dotted hierarchy connectors, expander, type icon, inline rename (double-click, F2/Return, arrows move row to row while editing), the middle bar (layer colour swatch with a layer picker, the viewport and render dots that cycle grey/green/red, Ctrl-click for the children, paint by dragging across rows, the enable tick/cross with Alt-click for the subtree, a look-through button on cameras) and tag chips (material, driver node, scatter); selected / last-selected / child-of-selected / hidden row states, Ctrl and Shift multi-select, middle-click selects the subtree; search that filters without selecting, a type filter, a Show menu (flat, by layer, sort, tags, three row heights) and a path bar with Set As Root; drag to reorder or reparent with Ctrl to copy; a full context menu

SceneObject::vis_viewport / vis_render (0 inherit, 1 on, 2 off) and enabled; object_visible / object_render_visible walk the parents with the C4D rule (grey inherits, green and red override in both directions, grey at the root is visible, layers and enabled still apply); a pre-dots file's visible=false loads as an explicit red dot; layers carry a colour

scene_move_object(from, to, new_parent) moves an object in the array and fixes every index that pointed into it - parents, selected, the multi-selection, the active and last-used cameras - and refuses a move under itself or a descendant

Animation tracks: per-key interpolation (linear, smooth, hold, bezier with auto-clamped / user / broken tangents), five extrapolation modes (constant, linear, cycle, cycle with offset, ping-pong), a modifier stack (noise, oscillator, offset, limit, smooth) and expressions (t, frame, fps, value, functions, other properties by path); the old track text form still loads, the new K2 form round-trips byte-identically

Curve operations behind the Timeline and Curve editor: move (colliding keys merge), retime about a pivot, mirror, smooth, flatten, ease presets incl. Easy Ease, bake one key per frame, simplify (Ramer-Douglas-Peucker), snap to frames, copy/paste relative to the first key
The document timeline: frame rate, range, preview range, loop mode, autokey, snap, markers; time formatted and parsed as frames, SMPTE timecode or seconds

Every property of every scene object (transform, squeeze, colour, visibility, deformers, scatter, light, camera optics, planet, infinite surface) and of the world (sun, sky, fog, water, clouds, terrain height) is animatable by path through one table; recording reads the live value, applying writes it back each frame, removing the last key makes the property static again; nothing moves unless it has a key
Object tracks, world tracks, the timeline settings and markers live in the scene file (undo snapshots carry them); an old file without them loads static at 30 fps

The Timeline: transport with previous/next key, frame field in the display mode, range/fps/loop/preview/autokey/every-frame/snap; ruler with ticks, preview band, draggable named markers, Ctrl-scrub snapping to keys; a track tree (owner > group > component, axis-coloured) with summary rows, key glyphs per interpolation, click/Ctrl/box select, drag with frame snapping, retime handles, copy/paste/duplicate/delete, ease and extrapolation menus, modifiers, double-click to add a key

The Curve editor: chosen tracks as value-against-time curves in axis colours, key and tangent-handle drags (Alt breaks a handle), speed (derivative) view, normalised view, ghost of the curve during a drag, Smooth/Flatten/Bake/Simplify tools, per-track expression field with live error, modifier rows

The animation circle beside every keyable property row (empty static, ring animated, filled keyed here; click/Ctrl/Shift/Ctrl+Shift), Autokey on edits, the keyframe navigator, K keys the selection's transform, right-click menu with ease/extrapolation/show-curve

Animation through the action schema and MCP: set_key/remove_key/remove_track/keys (with a reply), set_frame/play/stop/set_range, set_extrapolation/set_ease/set_interp, bake/simplify/snap_keys/mirror_keys/retime, set_expression/add_modifier/clear_modifiers, add_marker/remove_marker, key_transform, playblast; tracks addressed by object+prop, world, node+attr or id

Tool rows as Cinema 4D command palettes: square icon buttons on the 18/26/36 px ladder (Settings > General > Icon size), 2 px apart with 1 px rules between groups; the global palette (undo/redo, recompute, sculpt, move/rotate/scale, twist/bend/skew/taper, gizmos), each workspace's row (toolbar_tools.cpp), the viewport header and the Timeline transport

Languages: English built in (tagged dictionary + identity tags regenerated by tools/i18n_scan.py), resources/lang/<code>.json files listed in Settings > General and chosen by the preferences; German and French ship; a missing tag falls back to English then to the tag, distinct missing tags are counted; a malformed file fails with a reason and leaves English active; every tag a shipped file translates must exist in English

Mesh objects and their scattered copies are drawn into the sun's shadow map with their deformers, so rocks and trees cast shadows on the terrain, and meshes sample the map so they receive the terrain's and each other's shadows; the map is redrawn only when a mesh actually moved (a field-wise key, never struct bytes)
The selected object's animated position drawn in the viewport as a path through the play range with a cross per key
scene_state.json objects carry pos, rot, scale and an animated flag, and the state carries the timeline block and an op's reply, so a script can read back what an animation did
